notes:
Profile: SMB building a knowledge-centered chat overlay for support teams. Primary contact: CTO Elena Ramirez. Engineers running experiments on hosted API before committing to reserved capacity.

Observed problem: short, high-amplitude bursts from tenant replay cause 429s and degraded UX. Requests come from a single API key; their front-end batches user messages aggressively which amplifies concurrency.

Requests/asks from call: can Redwood provide recommended per-key concurrency thresholds, a small burst window for short spikes, and clear guidance on header values to implement friendly client-side backoff and in-app messaging? Also want a short doc snippet they can paste into front-end to detect 429 vs 503 vs transient timeouts.

Current mitigation: client-side exponential backoff with jitter; naive global queue on proxy. They want better server-side behavior or a recommended pattern for per-tenant throttles (switching to per-tenant keys) to avoid noisy-neighbor effect.

Cost sensitivity: want to avoid large monthly reserved spend; prefer pay-as-you-go with some burst headroom. Interested in Optimize tips to reduce tokens (system prompt compaction + caching frequent responses).

Security: SOC2 + SSO required for pilot customers; retention controls nice-to-have. No VPC planned.

Quote: "Our chat UI shows \"Too many requests\" to end-users during demo days — unacceptable. We need a graceful retry path and clear limits." — CTO Elena Ramirez.

Recommended AE action: send short FAQ on rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After), example front-end retry pseudo-code, and a proposal for a 30-day POC that includes a temporary burst allowance for two demo events.
